patch_description: Crossover of the two implementations. Parent A (prior program) achieves far fewer slope changes (48 vs 64) and fewer false reversals (35 vs 45) via a double zero-phase SG pass and a conservative slope-lead compensation, but has higher lag (0.35) and lower noise reduction (0.65). Parent B (current) achieves better lag (0.27), noise reduction (0.82) and correlation (0.97) via volatility-gated multi-scale SG. The hybrid keeps the shared Kalman+RTS core, then applies: (1) the volatility-gated multi-scale zero-phase SG from parent B (strong smoothing in volatile regions, preserving dynamics in quiet regions), (2) a short second zero-phase SG pass from parent A to further suppress spurious reversals where it matters most, and (3) a mild, conservative slope-lead compensation (scaled-down version of parent A's stage 4) to restore corner responsiveness, reducing lag without reintroducing noise. Output is end-aligned and trimmed to sliding-window length, same as both parents. All stages are O(n) convolutions; the heavy state-space loops are shared by both parents and unchanged.
